elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The chart shows Mongolia's total external debt from 2015 to 2025. Debt generally increased, from 24,117 in 2015 to 41,306 in 2025, with small intervening declines.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.description: The top bar divides total external debt into public and publicly guaranteed, private nonguaranteed, and short-term debt; private nonguaranteed is the largest. A shaded connector expands public and publicly guaranteed debt into multilateral, bilateral, and private creditors, of which bilateral is largest. Further shaded connectors expand multilateral debt into Asian Dev. Bank, World Bank-IDA, and other multilateral, and bilateral debt into China, Japan, and other bilateral. Asian Dev. Bank and China are the largest items in their respective breakdowns.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four panels show external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI from 2015 to 2025. Both debt service ratios rise to a pronounced peak before falling, while the external debt ratios fluctuate and generally decline toward the end. In 2025, external debt / exports is the highest printed ratio at 263%, and debt service / GNI is the lowest at 18%.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two boxes compare 2025 terms, with small bars beneath each measure. The official creditors box lists maturity of 23 years, grace period of 7 years, and interest rate of 4.0%; the private creditors box lists 4 years, 4 years, and 7.9%, respectively. Official commitments have longer maturity and grace periods, while private commitments have a higher interest rate.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
